statutes: State v. Anderson, 12 Kan. App. 2d 342, 744 P.2d 143 (1987)
legalName: Petition for Expungement of a Fulfilled Kansas Diversion Agreement under K.S.A. 21-6614

routeSelectionsMade.printedContext: I respectfully request of the Court an order of expungement of my [ ] conviction and related arrest records OR [ ] diversion record and related arrest records.
routeSelectionsMade.because: K.S.A. 21-6614(a)(2) is the diversion lane and is the route this family is built for. A petition built for one statutory route states which route it is.

routeSelectionsMade.printedContext: 8. (Select and complete either Option A or B, NOT both) — Option A.
routeSelectionsMade.because: Option B is the K.S.A. 21-6614(a)(3) specialty-court lane, which is a separate track with no waiting period and its own fee-waiver provision.

routeSelectionNote: Two elections, both determined by the statutory route and both guarded in the build path against a held answer that contradicts them. Every other control on these six forms is left unmarked, and each carries its own reason for this route in the field map.

participantFacingObligations.question: Which court does this go to?
participantFacingObligations.answer: File with the clerk of the district court, docketed in the original criminal action, with the Criminal Cover Sheet and the required number of copies.

participantFacingObligations.question: What does it cost?
participantFacingObligations.answer: Docket fee $176 under K.S.A. 21-6614(g)(2). The supreme court may additionally impose a charge not exceeding $19 per case to fund non-judicial personnel; 2026 Senate Bill 430 carries that authority from July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2030. The docket fee is the only fee that may be collected for the case.

participantFacingObligations.question: Can the fee be waived?
participantFacingObligations.answer: None in this lane. The only fee waiver in K.S.A. 21-6614 is the specialty court waiver at (a)(3). 2026 House Bill 2724, which would have authorised judges to waive the expungement docket fee on a poverty affidavit, died without enactment, so no general poverty-based statutory waiver exists. Some district courts nonetheless accept a poverty affidavit in practice.

participantFacingObligations.question: Who gets notice, and who sends it?
participantFacingObligations.answer: The court sets the hearing date and causes notice to be given to the prosecutor and the arresting law enforcement agency, K.S.A. 21-6614(g)(1).

participantFacingObligations.question: Is any waiting-period lane closed on this route?
participantFacingObligations.answer: The second or subsequent DUI lanes are not offered on this route. K.S.A. 21-6614(d)(2) does not reach a diversion, and the Judicial Council chart records the 7-year and 10-year rows as not applicable in the diversion column.

participantFacingObligations.question: What date does the clock run from?
participantFacingObligations.answer: The triggering event is fulfilment of the diversion terms, and nothing else.

participantFacingObligations.question: Do I serve anybody?
participantFacingObligations.answer: The participant files the Notice of Hearing with the original plus two copies and the clerk sends them. The participant does not serve and does not sign the certificate.

participantFacingObligations.question: Do I sign anything, and is it sworn?
participantFacingObligations.answer: The petitioner signs the petition under penalty of perjury.

participantFacingObligations.question: Is there anything that stops this route entirely?
participantFacingObligations.answer: A person required to register under the Kansas Offender Registration Act may not expunge any conviction or any part of their criminal record while registration is required, K.S.A. 21-6614(f). That freezes every case in the record, not only the registrable offence. The sole exception is the K.S.A. 22-4908 drug offender route; sex offender and violent offender registrants are barred with no exception.

selectionControls.reasonForThisControlOnThisRoute: The route determines this election. This packet is the K.S.A. 21-6614(a)(2) diversion route, and a petition built for one statutory route states which route it is rather than asking the petitioner. The held disposition is a fulfilled diversion agreement and the build refuses to run if it is anything else.

selectionControls.label: Item 8 — Option A (selection)

Option B is the K.S.A. 21-6614(a)(3) specialty-court lane, which is its own track; the K.S.A. 21-6614(a)(1) conviction route this packet is built for is Option A. The build refuses to run over a held answer that a specialty-court programme was completed, or that a felony conviction or pending felony proceeding exists, because Option A asserts the opposite.

boundaryRefusals.reason: the participant marks the "ten" box at item 8.A.i themselves: which of the four waiting periods applies turns on how the offence is classified in the Kansas sentencing grid and on the date the offence was committed, and the committed registry says LegalEase "does not assert that the participant is eligible, does not classify the offence into a grid severity level for them"
boundaryRefusals.why: the participant marks the "ten" box at item 8.A.i themselves: which of the four waiting periods applies turns on how the offence is classified in the Kansas sentencing grid and on the date the offence was committed, and the committed registry says LegalEase "does not assert that the participant is eligible, does not classify the offence into a grid severity level for them"
boundaryRefusals.participantMustSupply: mark this box only if ten years have elapsed since your date of final discharge AND the ten-year period is the one your offence falls into. Which period applies depends on how your offence is classified; the Judicial Council chart printed on pages 5 and 6 of this petition works it through, and the packet does not classify the offence for you.
boundaryRefusals.whyTheRouteCannotDetermineIt: The route is K.S.A. 21-6614(a)(2) for every one of the four boxes; what differs between them is the severity classification of the conduct the diversion was entered for and the date the offence was committed, which are facts of the case. The committed track registry states in terms that LegalEase does not classify the offence into a grid severity level, and under State v. Anderson the law in effect when the offence was committed governs. On this route the committed record additionally records that the ten-year lane at K.S.A. 21-6614(d)(2) does not reach a diversion at all and that the Judicial Council chart shows not-applicable in the diversion column for the seven-year and ten-year DUI rows. Marking one of these boxes from the route alone would be asserting a legal characterisation of a code section on a petition sworn under penalty of perjury.

boundaryRefusals.effectiveLabel: Item 8 — Option B, specialty court programme (selection)
boundaryRefusals.printedLabel: Item 8 — Option B, specialty court programme (selection)
boundaryRefusals.reason: Option B is the K.S.A. 21-6614(a)(3) specialty-court lane and a different track
boundaryRefusals.why: Option B is the K.S.A. 21-6614(a)(3) specialty-court lane and a different track
boundaryRefusals.routeConditionThatMakesItInapplicable: Item 8 says to select and complete either Option A or Option B, NOT both. This packet is the K.S.A. 21-6614(a)(1) conviction route and states Option A; Option B is the specialty-court lane under K.S.A. 21-6614(a)(3), which has no waiting period, its own fee-waiver provision and its own findings, and is a separate track.
